findings.title: Backup code consumption is non-atomic (race allows reuse)
findings.body: The backup code check reads user.backupCodes, nulls the matching entry in memory, then writes the array back with no compare-and-swap or transaction. Two concurrent logins with the same code both pass the check before either update lands, so one 'single-use' code can open multiple sessions. A concurrent use of a different code can also be overwritten by the last write, which revives a code that was already consumed.

findings.title: Unvalidated backupCode string can match nulled entries or throw
findings.body: `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll` is called on raw input. Used codes are stored as `null`, so the check relies on indexOf of a string never matching null. That holds today, but the input is never validated for length or format. `replaceAll` also needs ES2021; on older runtimes this throws, and the user sees a generic error instead of a proper message.

findings.title: Backup codes screen can be dismissed without onEnable
findings.body: On the DisplayBackupCodes step, 2FA is already enabled on the server. If the dialog is closed through onOpenChange (Escape key or overlay click) instead of the Close button, onEnable and resetState never run. The parent UI then shows 2FA as disabled while it is actually on. The step also stays at DisplayBackupCodes the next time the modal opens.

findings.title: Non-string backupCode in request body causes 500
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` assumes a string. Any other truthy value (a number, an array) throws an unhandled exception and returns a 500 instead of a 400 validation error.

findings.title: formatBackupCode used before its const declaration
findings.body: handleSetup calls `formatBackupCode`, which is declared later in the component body as a `const`. This only works because handleSetup runs asynchronously after render. It is fragile: an early call would throw a temporal dead zone error.

findings.title: No tests for logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code
findings.body: The new authentication paths are untested: backup-code login, single-use enforcement, incorrect code, and disabling 2FA with a backup code. The PR leaves only a TODO comment for these cases.
